result.topic_en: Euler's fragments on products and transformations of quadratic forms of the type $a\alpha x^2+b\beta y^2$, on divisors of $x^2+ny^2$ having the same form, on the form of the primes $4na\pm b^2$, and on the quotient when $mnff+gg$ has a prime divisor of the form $(maa+nbb)/\Delta$.
result.transcription:
160 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.

Theorema. Si formula $a\alpha pp+b\beta qq$ ducatur in formulam $abrr+\alpha\beta ss$, productum erit:
$ab(a\alpha pprr+\beta\beta qqss)+\alpha\beta(a\alpha ppss+bbqqrr)=ab(apr\pm\beta qs)^2+\alpha\beta(\alpha ps\pm bqr)^2$,
hujus ergo producti forma est $abxx+\alpha\beta yy$ existente $x=apr\pm\beta qs$ et $y=\alpha ps\pm bqr$.
(Conf. pro casu $a=b=1$ Comment. arithm. T. II, p. 201.)

Problema. Formulam $a\alpha xx+b\beta yy$ in aliam ejusdem generis transformare.
Solutio. Ponatur $x=bmp+\beta nq$ et $y=anp-\alpha mq$ et prodibit
$a\alpha bbmmpp+a\alpha\beta\beta nnqq+b\beta aannpp+b\beta\alpha\alpha mmqq=abmm(abpp+\alpha\beta qq)+\alpha\beta nn(\alpha\beta qq+abpp)=$
$(abmm+\alpha\beta nn)(abpp+\alpha\beta qq)$.
A. m. T. I. p. 130.

7.
(N. Fuss I.)

Theorema. Si numerus formae $xx+nyy$ divisibilis fuerit per numerum $pp+nqq$, quotus semper erit numerus ejusdem formae $A^2+nB^2$.
Demonstratio. Cum numeri $x$ et $y$ ad $pp+nqq$ debeant esse primi, et $p$ et $q$ quoque sint primi inter se, quicunque fuerint numeri $x$ et $y$, semper per $p$ et $q$ ita repraesentari possunt, ut sit $x=\alpha p+\beta q$ et $y=\gamma p+\delta q$. Hoc modo formula $xx+nyy$ abit in hanc: $pp(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)+qq(\beta\beta+n\delta\delta)+2pq(\alpha\beta+n\gamma\delta)$, quae per $pp+nqq$ divisa praebeat quotum $\Delta$, ita ut sit
$pp(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)+qq(\beta\beta+n\delta\delta)+2pq(\alpha\beta+n\gamma\delta)=\Delta pp+n\Delta qq$.
Hinc igitur patet fore $\Delta=\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma$, $n\Delta=\beta\beta+n\delta\delta$ et $\alpha\beta+n\gamma\delta=0$, unde jam patet formam ipsius $\Delta$ esse $\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma$. Tum etiam erit $n\Delta=\beta\beta+n\delta\delta$ et $\alpha\beta+n\gamma\delta=0$. Ex ultima fit $\frac{\beta}{\delta}=\frac{-n\gamma}{\alpha}$. Ponatur ergo
$\delta=\alpha f$ et $\beta=-n\gamma f$, erit $\beta\beta+n\delta\delta=nff(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)=n\Delta$, unde $\Delta=ff(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)$.
Cum igitur sit $\Delta=\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma$, sequitur fore $f=\pm1$. His valoribus fit
$x=\alpha p\mp n\gamma q$ et $y=\gamma p\pm\alpha q$.
Hinc fit $xx+nyy=pp(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)+nqq(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)=(pp+nqq)(\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma)$,
sicque quotus uti jam vidimus $\Delta=\alpha\alpha+n\gamma\gamma$.
A. m. T. III. p. 184.

8.

Theoremata demonstranda. I. Si fuerit $4na+bb$ numerus primus, erit semper hujus formae $xx-ayy$.
II. Si fuerit $4na-bb$ numerus primus, erit semper hujus formae $ayy-xx$.
A. m. T. II. p. 154.

9.

Theorema. Si numerus $mnff+gg$ divisorem habeat primum $p=\frac{maa+nbb}{\Delta}$, tum etiam quotus $q$, ex hac divisione ortus, erit quoque ejusdem formae scilicet $q=\frac{mcc+ndd}{\Delta}$.
Explicatio. Quaerantur primo duo numeri $\lambda$ et $\mu$, ut sit $\lambda a-\mu p=\pm1$; deinde ut formula $mnff+gg$ divisorem admittat $p$, alteram litteram $f$ pro lubitu accipere licet, tum vero altera $g$ ita esse debet comparata, ut sit $g=n\lambda bf-\nu p$, quibus notatis cum sit $mnff+gg=pq$ existente $q=\frac{mcc+ndd}{\Delta}$, litterae $c$ et $d$ sequenti modo determinantur
$c=n\mu bf-\nu a$ et $d=m\mu af+\nu b-\lambda\Delta f$.
A. m. T. II. p. 211.

items.quote: Si formula $a\alpha pp+b\beta qq$ ducatur in formulam $abrr+\alpha\beta ss$, productum erit
items.english: If the formula $a\alpha pp+b\beta qq$ is multiplied by the formula $abrr+\alpha\beta ss$, the product will be [of the form $abxx+\alpha\beta yy$].

items.quote: Formulam $a\alpha xx+b\beta yy$ in aliam ejusdem generis transformare.
items.english: To transform the formula $a\alpha xx+b\beta yy$ into another of the same kind.

items.quote: Si numerus formae $xx+nyy$ divisibilis fuerit per numerum $pp+nqq$, quotus semper erit numerus ejusdem formae $A^2+nB^2$.
items.english: If a number of the form $xx+nyy$ is divisible by a number $pp+nqq$, the quotient will always be a number of the same form $A^2+nB^2$.

items.quote: I. Si fuerit $4na+bb$ numerus primus, erit semper hujus formae $xx-ayy$.
items.english: Theorems to be proved. I. If $4na+bb$ is a prime number, it will always be of the form $xx-ayy$.

items.quote: II. Si fuerit $4na-bb$ numerus primus, erit semper hujus formae $ayy-xx$.
items.english: II. If $4na-bb$ is a prime number, it will always be of the form $ayy-xx$.

items.quote: Si numerus $mnff+gg$ divisorem habeat primum $p=\frac{maa+nbb}{\Delta}$, tum etiam quotus $q$, ex hac divisione ortus, erit quoque ejusdem formae scilicet $q=\frac{mcc+ndd}{\Delta}$.
items.english: If the number $mnff+gg$ has a prime divisor $p=\frac{maa+nbb}{\Delta}$, then the quotient $q$ arising from this division will also be of the same form, namely $q=\frac{mcc+ndd}{\Delta}$.
